questions.q: What was unusual about the room where Captain Hoseason sat at the inn?
choices: It was crowded with maps, charts and sea chests
It was full of sailors singing and drinking punch
It was heated like an oven by a great coal fire
It was dark and cold with every window boarded
questions.evidence: heated like an oven by a great fire of coal

questions.q: Why did the captain say he kept his room so hot?
choices: He had cold blood from his years in the tropic seas
He had a fever he had caught on his last long voyage
He was trying to dry out his wet sea-clothes quickly
He wanted his visitors to feel tired and sleepy
questions.evidence: I'm a cold-rife man by my nature

questions.q: Why did David leave his uncle alone with the captain?
choices: The captain asked him to carry a letter to the pier
Ransome begged him to come and see the ship's boat
His uncle sent him to fetch the lawyer Mr. Rankeillor
He wanted a look at the sea and the room was too close
questions.evidence: so sickened by the closeness of the room

questions.q: What was new to David when he walked down on the beach?
choices: The seaweeds, some with little bladders that crackled
The great waves crashing loudly on the rocks
The crabs and shells left behind by the tide
The white sand stretching for miles along the shore
questions.evidence: some with little bladders that crackled between my fingers

questions.q: What did David offer Ransome instead of the bowl of punch he wanted?
choices: A glass of ale
A cup of milk
A dish of porridge
Some hot tea
questions.evidence: But a glass of ale you may have, and welcome

questions.q: What did the landlord say about Mr. Rankeillor?
choices: He was a very honest man
He was a cruel and greedy lawyer
He had left the county for good
He was a friend of Ebenezer's

questions.q: The landlord says David has "a kind of gliff of Mr. Alexander." Using the note in the text, what does "gliff" mean?
choices: Look
Voice
Walk
Temper

questions.q: According to the landlord, what was the report that went around about Ebenezer?
choices: That he had killed his brother Alexander to get the place
That he had sold his own land to Captain Hoseason
That he had married Jennet Clouston and then left her
That he had stolen gold from the kirk at Cramond parish
questions.evidence: just that he had killed him

questions.q: What did David learn when the landlord said Alexander was the eldest son?
choices: That the house of Shaws should rightly belong to David
That his father had been a sailor before he was a teacher
That Mr. Rankeillor had always cheated the Balfour family
That his uncle was really much younger than he looked
questions.evidence: was now one of the rich of the earth

questions.q: David says the captain "was two men." What does he mean?
choices: He seemed good on land but became worse once on board
He had a twin brother who sailed with him on the brig
He was both the captain and the navigator of the ship
He could talk like a Scot and also like an Englishman
questions.evidence: left the better one behind as soon as he set foot on board his vessel

questions.q: What did the captain whisper in David's ear to get him on board?
choices: That Mr. Rankeillor was waiting aboard the brig
That there was a gift for him in the cabin below
To take care of the old tod, who meant mischief
That he knew a secret about David's dead father
questions.evidence: Take care of the old tod;* he means mischief

questions.q: What did David see when he ran to the ship's side?
choices: Ransome swimming back to the pier with the captain's letter
His uncle climbing up the ship's ladder to join him on deck
Mr. Rankeillor waving to him from the end of the town pier
The boat pulling for the town with his uncle in the stern
questions.evidence: with my uncle sitting in the stern

questions.q: What happened to David right after he cried out for help?
choices: He was tied to the mast with ropes
He was locked in the captain's cabin
He jumped overboard into the sea
He was struck and fell senseless
questions.evidence: I saw a great flash of fire, and fell senseless

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: David learns the sea is dangerous and decides to stay safe on shore
David and the captain become friends and plan a voyage together
David visits the lawyer and claims the house of Shaws as his own
David is tricked aboard the Covenant and kidnapped with his uncle's help
